issues.label: Jurisdiction and finality posture
issues.why: The court must confirm it has authority to decide reserved child support and property issues after a bifurcated decree.

issues.label: Scope of reserved issues
issues.why: The court must ensure it only adjudicates matters expressly reserved in the April 2022 decree/stipulation.

issues.label: Enforce stipulation reimbursements
issues.why: The court must implement the $61,690 repair reimbursement term and determine its effect on the estate division accounting.

issues.label: Rule 90.3 applicability period
issues.why: The court must determine the correct time period for child support owed through high school graduation under Civil Rule 90.3.

issues.label: Child support retroactivity limits
issues.why: The court must address whether, and to what extent, past support can be awarded for periods before filing or before adjudication.

issues.label: Custody type for 90.3 formula
issues.why: The court must decide whether primary/shared/divided/hybrid custody applies when the child resides in a facility rather than with a parent.

issues.label: Primary physical custody finding
issues.why: A valid Rule 90.3 order requires explicit findings identifying which parent had primary physical custody (or why an alternative approach is used).

issues.label: Meaning of 'physical custody'
issues.why: The court must interpret whether legal guardianship, decision-making, and visitation constitute physical custody when placement is state/facility-based.

issues.label: State custody and support duty
issues.why: The court must decide how a child’s placement “under the care of the State” affects parents’ ongoing support obligations.

issues.label: Third-party payor offsets
issues.why: The court must determine whether government benefits or state payments offset or alter parental support calculations.

issues.label: Child’s special needs impacts
issues.why: The court must consider disability-related expenses and whether deviations from standard support are justified.

issues.label: Rule 90.3 deviation findings
issues.why: If deviating from guideline support, the court must make the specific written findings required by Rule 90.3(c).

issues.label: Adjusted annual income findings
issues.why: The court must make support income findings supported by the record, including what constitutes “adjusted annual income.”

issues.label: Income attribution/imputation
issues.why: The court must decide whether to impute income given job change, earning capacity, or voluntary underemployment.

issues.label: Treatment of new job evidence
issues.why: The court must determine whether late-disclosed employment changes should affect income calculations and whether additional evidence is needed.

issues.label: Allowable deductions under 90.3
issues.why: The court must correctly apply taxes, mandatory deductions, and other permitted adjustments to income.

issues.label: Support when child turns 18
issues.why: The court must apply Rule 90.3’s post-18/high-school graduation termination provisions and identify the exact end date.

issues.label: Post-majority support authority
issues.why: The court must identify the legal basis (statute/case law/equity) for ordering support after majority for a disabled adult child.

issues.label: Standard for adult-child support
issues.why: The court must determine the governing standard for amount/duration of support for an incapacitated adult child.

issues.label: Allocation method for adult support
issues.why: The court must decide whether to use Rule 90.3, a needs-based approach, or another method for post-majority support.

issues.label: Need and expense findings
issues.why: The court must make findings that the claimed $1,280/month expenses are reasonable, necessary, and attributable to the child.

issues.label: Treatment of room and board
issues.why: The court must decide what portion of facility costs are included/excluded and how anticipated Social Security coverage affects support.

issues.label: Contingent end point clarity
issues.why: The court must specify clear triggering conditions (e.g., Social Security approval) and whether modification is required when benefits begin.

issues.label: Support payee designation
issues.why: The court must determine whether payments should be made to Duckett, to the facility, to a trust, or for the daughter’s benefit given guardianship.

issues.label: Guardian/conservator role
issues.why: The court must account for Duckett’s legal authority and fiduciary duties when ordering and directing support payments.

issues.label: Medical/therapy expense allocation
issues.why: The court must decide responsibility for uninsured medical/therapy costs and whether they are included in the ordered amount.

issues.label: Arrearage calculation accuracy
issues.why: The court must calculate any past-due support precisely and include interest if required.

issues.label: Support order enforceability terms
issues.why: The court must include legally enforceable terms (amount, frequency, duration) rather than precatory encouragement.

issues.label: Modification standards preserved
issues.why: The court must clarify that future changes (benefits, needs, income) are addressed via modification standards and procedures.

issues.label: Property identification completeness
issues.why: The court must identify all assets and debts in the marital estate, including trust-held sale proceeds.

issues.label: Valuation date selection
issues.why: The court must choose and justify valuation dates for real property, proceeds, and debts (separation, trial, or other).

issues.label: Valuation method adequacy
issues.why: The court must ensure valuation evidence/methods are reliable and findings are supported by the record.

issues.label: Separate vs marital classification
issues.why: The court must classify disputed items (e.g., inheritance/loan forgiveness/check) under Alaska marital property principles.

issues.label: Burden of proof on separate property
issues.why: The court must apply the correct burden and standard for proving an asset is separate and traceable.

issues.label: Inheritance characterization
issues.why: The court must decide whether the $100,000 early inheritance is separate, partially separate, or marital based on intent and use.

issues.label: Gift vs loan forgiveness analysis
issues.why: The court must distinguish between forgiveness of marital debt and a separate gift to one spouse and allocate effects accordingly.

issues.label: Donor intent relevance
issues.why: The court must weigh and make findings on the mother’s intent and whether it controls classification in light of transmutation/commingling.

issues.label: Commingling and transmutation
issues.why: The court must determine whether depositing the $50,000 into a joint account transmuted it into marital property.

issues.label: Tracing commingled funds
issues.why: The court must decide whether the separate portion can be traced notwithstanding commingling and how to value any separate component.

issues.label: Marital debt treatment
issues.why: The court must allocate responsibility for debts, including the original $150,000 obligation and its payoff/forgiveness effects.

issues.label: Waste/dissipation claim handling
issues.why: The court must decide whether Cline’s post-separation scam loss constitutes dissipation affecting the equitable division.

issues.label: Dissipation standards and proof
issues.why: If dissipation is alleged, the court must apply the legal standard (fault, intent, reasonableness) and make findings.

issues.label: Merrill factors application
issues.why: The court must apply Merrill factors correctly to reach an equitable (not necessarily equal) division.

issues.label: Merrill findings sufficiency
issues.why: The court must make adequate findings on relevant Merrill factors to permit appellate review.

issues.label: Earning capacity comparisons
issues.why: The court must assess future earning potential and whether it justifies a 55/45 split.

issues.label: Homemaker contribution weight
issues.why: The court must consider non-economic contributions and whether they justify an unequal division.

issues.label: Health and age considerations
issues.why: The court must address parties’ health/age as they bear on equitable distribution.

issues.label: Financial condition at division
issues.why: The court must consider each party’s current financial condition, including income stability and assets received.

issues.label: Equitable division arithmetic
issues.why: The court must ensure the property allocation totals match the intended percentages after reimbursements, credits, and tax allocations.

issues.label: Treatment of trust-held proceeds
issues.why: The court must decide how to distribute funds held in trust and what obligations are paid from them before distribution.

issues.label: Capital gains tax classification
issues.why: The court must determine whether tax liabilities from marital asset sales are marital debts and how they should be allocated.

issues.label: Capital gains tax allocation method
issues.why: The court must decide whether to allocate taxes pro rata, pay from trust first, or offset via property division adjustments.

issues.label: Tax amount certainty
issues.why: The court must determine whether tax liability is known/estimable and whether to reserve jurisdiction for final accounting.

issues.label: Tax payment timing mechanics
issues.why: The court must specify when and how taxes are paid (from trust or by parties) to avoid enforcement ambiguity.

issues.label: Ramsey credit legal standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard for post-separation payments to preserve marital property (Ramsey credits).

issues.label: Evidentiary support for credits
issues.why: The court must decide whether Cline proved the amounts, purpose, and necessity of claimed preservation expenditures.

issues.label: Credit vs reimbursement vs division
issues.why: The court must decide whether such payments warrant a credit, are accounted for in valuation, or are treated as voluntary.

issues.label: Offsets for exclusive use/benefit
issues.why: The court must consider whether any credit should be offset by a party’s exclusive use of an asset or other benefits received.

issues.label: Interaction with repair stipend
issues.why: The court must avoid double counting between the stipulated $61,690 repairs reimbursement and additional claimed Ramsey credits.

issues.label: Burden and documentation for credits
issues.why: The court must apply the correct burden of proof and address missing documentation or credibility issues.

issues.label: Reconsideration legal standard
issues.why: The court must apply the proper standard for reconsideration and identify whether asserted errors are factual, legal, or newly discovered.

issues.label: Need for additional findings
issues.why: The court must determine whether post-trial motion issues require supplemental findings to support custody/support/property rulings.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: The court must resolve conflicting testimony (expenses, intent, payments) and explain material credibility choices.

issues.label: Due process and notice
issues.why: The court must ensure each party had fair notice and opportunity to litigate late-raised issues (new job, taxes, credits).

issues.label: Form of final judgment
issues.why: The court must enter a clear final order/judgment specifying amounts, deadlines, and distribution steps for enforceability.

issues.label: Attorney’s fees considerations
issues.why: The court must consider whether to award divorce attorney’s fees under Alaska’s relative economic circumstances approach if requested.

issues.label: Interest on monetary awards
issues.why: The court must determine whether statutory interest applies to reimbursements, equalization payments, or arrearages.

issues.label: Reservation of jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must decide whether to retain jurisdiction to adjust support/tax allocations when Social Security or final tax figures are determined.
